Taiwan Imposes Temporary Export Restrictions on Select Semiconductor Products

TAIPEI, June 7 — Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs has imposed temporary export restrictions on select semiconductor products, citing concerns over national security and the protection of critical technology. The measure, implemented earlier this week, immediately affected shipments of advanced microchips and manufacturing equipment, disrupting operations for several companies in the sector.

The restrictions, which apply to certain high-end logic chips and equipment used in their production, have already begun to affect companies such as Chang Wah Technology Co Ltd, a major supplier of semiconductor packaging materials. “We are closely monitoring the situation. Several of our scheduled shipments to overseas clients are on hold pending further clarification from authorities,” a spokesperson for Chang Wah Technology Co Ltd said Friday.

The ministry stated that the export controls are “temporary and targeted,” aiming to prevent unauthorized transfer of sensitive technology. “We understand the impact this has on local industry, but safeguarding Taiwan’s technological edge is of paramount importance,” Deputy Minister Lee Hsien-chung told reporters.

Industry analysts say the move has created uncertainty among semiconductor manufacturers, with many companies reassessing their supply chains and order commitments. “There’s immediate concern about contract fulfillment and revenue projections, especially for firms heavily reliant on foreign sales,” said Lin Shu-jen, an analyst at Taipei-based research firm TechTrends Consulting.

According to the Taiwan Semiconductor Industry Association, the restrictions could affect up to 15 percent of the sector’s monthly export volume if they remain in place. “We urge the government to provide clear guidance and a timeline for review, as prolonged uncertainty could erode global customer confidence,” the association said in a statement.

The ministry has not indicated when the export restrictions might be lifted. Companies continue to seek clarification as shipments remain on hold and production schedules are adjusted in response.
